sector.narrative: Support for feminist, women-led and women's rights organisations and movements, and institutions (governmental and non-govermental) at all levels to enhance their effectiveness, influence and substainability (activities and core-funding). These organisations exist to bring about transformative change for gender equality and/or the rights of women and girls in developing countries. Their activities include agenda-setting, advocacy, policy dialogue, capacity development, awareness raising and prevention, service provision, conflict-prevention and peacebuilding, research, organising, and alliance and network building

Annual capacity building workshops for editors, reporters & bloggers to support alternative media narratives and platforms; 1 annual summit (year 5)

(i) 2 media training conducted by Akili Dada in Kisumu and Mombasa counties addressing biases in GBV reporting; exploring oppression and marginalization of women media and forging partnerships to amplify GBV work in the community. Each training had 20 media practitioners. (ii) CWID constituents have facilitated sessions with young women and youth groups in informal settlements on prevention of SGBV, sexual harassment and exploitation. (iii) CWID constituents taking lead in community initiatives with village elders educating on legal frameworks (SoA, penal code, CoK) and case management, CWID Consituents have taken lead in the meetings. (iv) CWID constituents engaging religious leaders (churches) on identification of sexual abuse and prevention of SGBV. (v) CWID YW alumni Initiating Football tournament with teenagers on comprehensive sex education (sexual hygiene, body autonomy). (vi) NGAA DADA: Engaged 79 women and men (77 females and 2 male) on a two day’s forum on an in-depth discussion on how the effects of climate change exacerbate Sexual Gender Based Violence and the importance of safeguarding women and girl’s rights in the event of calamities such as floods. (vii) Engaged 69 participants (46 females and 23 male) during a public awareness forum (Wezesha Dada) on the emerging trends of GBV and changing societal attitudes and perception towards Gender Based Violence.

Young women were provided with an opportunity and engaged in the local radio talk show towards sensitizing the community in the fight against SGBV/GBV. This was an interactive session in which the community called in to ask questions and sought clarifications (on SGBV/GBV matters. One of the listeners, Rajab Mumbo wanted to know who bears the burden of parental responsibility between the mother and the father. Kadii, the young women's leader in the WGG project present in the talk show, responded by saying that both parents bear equal responsibility in raising their children.
